providers.title: Normalization of PSD factorizations
providers.scope: A nonzero nonnegative matrix with entries at most B and a PSD factorization of size r_0 has a PSD factorization of some size r <= r_0 with tr F_i <= B and tr G_j <= r. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Affine certificates
providers.scope: If an affine subspace L of symmetric w x w matrices contains a positive definite matrix and an affine function is nonnegative on the positive semidefinite part of L, it equals <F, Y> + mu on L with F positive semidefinite and mu >= 0. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Semidefinite lifts give PSD factorizations
providers.scope: If a convex set with at least two points has a semidefinite lift of size r, every matrix of values of affine functions nonnegative on the set at points of the set has PSD rank at most r + 1. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exponential PSD rank of the shifted matching matrices (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There is c > 0 such that for every 0 < rho < 1 the matrix with entries |M ∩ δ(U)| − 1 + rho, on odd sets U and perfect matchings M of K_n, has PSD rank at least 2^(cn) for all large even n; proved in the sixth lesson. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Semidefinite lifts of the perfect matching polytope (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For all large even n, every semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope of K_n has size at least 2^(c_0 n); proved in the sixth lesson. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Large invariant subspaces
providers.scope: For even k >= 6 and w in {k/2, k/2+1}, every nonzero S_k-invariant space of functions on the w-subsets of [k] orthogonal to the constants has dimension at least k/2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local averaging
providers.scope: Averages over the restrictions of a cut to a cell, with random terminals and internal matching, have uniform marginal and variance at most theta_d(k) = 2^((d+10)/2) k^(-1/4) (1 + log k)^(1/2) times the variance, in every matrix dimension. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two positive semidefinite matrices
providers.scope: For positive semidefinite A, B and the projection P onto the nonnegative eigenspaces of A - B, tr(AB) >= ||PBP||^2 + ||QAQ||^2 with Q = I - P. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Orthogonal splitting
providers.scope: Positive semidefinite A_1, ..., A_L admit mutually orthogonal projections P_s with sum I such that the sum over s != z of ||P_s A_z P_s||^2 is at most 2^(L-1) times the sum of the overlaps tr(A_z A_z'), in every dimension. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Translation by a character
providers.scope: Multiplying a function whose Fourier coefficients vanish beyond block distance D from q by the character chi_q gives block degree at most D and keeps its square. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fourier smoothing of matrix squares
providers.scope: A product average of a positive semidefinite matrix function through channels with uniform marginals and variance factor theta is a sum of squares whose Fourier coefficients satisfy a bound weighted by lambda^dist, when L lambda^2 2^(L-1) theta <= 1. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Expanding multigraphs
providers.scope: For every even t there is a bipartite 100-regular multigraph on t vertices in which every vertex set W has at least min(|W|, t - |W|) edges leaving it. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A functional separating low-degree squares
providers.scope: On an odd parity system on such a multigraph there is a linear functional D with D(1) = 1, nonnegative on squares of block degree at most t/1000, equal to -epsilon on the disagreement count minus epsilon, and bounded by L^t times the sup norm. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Realization by odd cuts and matchings
providers.scope: For cells with terminals joined along the parity graph, every odd cut in the support of the product restriction crosses the matching exactly at the disagreeing edges. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniform smoothing of matching averages (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For a fixed number of cells and K > 0 there is d with ||T_t(I - Pi_d)|| <= N^(-K) for all cell sizes and admissible tables, and T_t Pi_d f is one polynomial of degree at most d in the counts between the cells. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The fourth moment
providers.scope: tr((T_t^* T_t)^2) <= e^(2a) (N+1)^b with a = l(l+1) + 1 and b = 2a + l^2, uniformly in the table. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dimensions outside the edge-product span
providers.scope: For N >= 4d^2, every irreducible subrepresentation of the complexified orthogonal complement of the products of at most d edge indicators has dimension at least N^(d/2)/(2^d d!). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Containment probabilities
providers.scope: A uniform matching with a given table contains a given set of disjoint edges with probability 2^(sum m_uu) prod (t_uv)_(m_uv) / prod (s_u)_(a_u). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
